topics.label: Course introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: These introductory remarks welcome the students and set out the course scope and lecture objectives.

topics.label: Biological mechanisms of cancer and experimental models
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain cancer as a multistep breakdown of normal cellular differentiation and tissue architecture alongside the experimental systems used to study it.

topics.label: Tumour invasion, metastasis, and histological progression
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how tumours transition from localized benign lesions to invasive and metastatic malignancies using histological and clinical examples.

topics.label: Tumour nomenclature, behaviour, and mechanisms of morbidity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address the naming conventions for tumours and examine how both benign and malignant growths cause clinical harm and mortality.

topics.label: Tumour incidence and comparative oncology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine cancer frequency across human populations and other animal species to frame cancer as a universal disease of multicellular organisms.

topics.label: Principles and practice of cancer screening
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss the clinical rationale for early cancer detection and evaluate screening approaches and limitations across different organ sites.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and practical reminders
topics.groupedBecause: These concluding remarks summarize the session and provide administrative reminders about revision and upcoming practical classes.
